topic: SAP Certified Associate - Generative AI Developer (C_AIG_2412) exam preparation - building, grounding, and operationalizing generative AI on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) using Generative AI Hub, the Orchestration Service, the SAP Cloud SDK for AI, prompt engineering, and retrieval-augmented generation with document grounding
cert_name: SAP Certified Associate - Generative AI Developer
exam_format: System-Based Assessment (SyBA): a single hands-on, task/activity-based assessment delivered in a live SAP system rather than a traditional multiple-choice test. Passing score is 76%. Delivered in English via SAP Certification Hub / Pearson VUE or as part of an SAP Learning subscription. Candidates should confirm the current question count, duration, and fee on SAP's official certification page, as SAP updates these per release (the 2412 version reflects the December 2024 release and is current for 2026).
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE' - NOTE the real exam is a System-Based Assessment (hands-on tasks), so frame practice questions to teach the same decisions and procedures a SyBA task would require
audience: Developers and SAP BTP practitioners who build generative AI applications on SAP BTP using Generative AI Hub, the Orchestration Service, and the SAP Cloud SDK for AI. Candidates should have hands-on SAP BTP experience, basic Python or JavaScript/CAP familiarity, and an understanding of LLM and prompt-engineering concepts. Aimed at the SAP ecosystem (consultants, BTP developers, SAP partners) where there is almost no competing Udemy prep content.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Foundations of SAP Business AI and Large Language Models
domains.notes: SAP Business AI strategy and landscape, how generative AI fits into SAP BTP, LLM fundamentals (tokens, context windows, temperature, embeddings), model families available in SAP Generative AI Hub, and core concepts of generative vs predictive AI. Responsible AI and SAP's AI ethics principles. Where Generative AI Hub, Orchestration, and the Cloud SDK for AI sit in the BTP architecture.

domains.name: Prompt engineering fundamentals and techniques
domains.notes: Prompt design patterns (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, role/system prompting), structuring prompts for reliable outputs, controlling format and JSON outputs, reducing hallucination, and iterating on prompts. Techniques specific to SAP business scenarios (summarization, extraction, classification, drafting) and evaluating prompt quality.

domains.name: The Generative AI Hub and Orchestration Service
domains.notes: Using Generative AI Hub in SAP AI Core / AI Launchpad to access and deploy foundation models; the Orchestration Service as the unified entry point - templating, model configuration, content filtering, data masking, and grounding modules chained in an orchestration workflow. Configuring harmonized access across model providers and switching models without rewriting application code.

domains.name: Prompt development, registry, and templates
domains.notes: Developing, versioning, and reusing prompts via the prompt registry and prompt templates; parameterized templates, template management, and promoting prompts across environments. Integrating templated prompts into applications and orchestration pipelines.

domains.name: Building and evaluating with the SAP Cloud SDK for AI
domains.notes: Using the SAP Cloud SDK for AI (Python and JavaScript/TypeScript) to call Generative AI Hub and the Orchestration Service from applications, implement chat/completions, function/tool calling, and streaming. Evaluating generative outputs for quality and safety, handling errors and limits, and integrating with SAP CAP applications on BTP.

domains.name: Grounding, RAG, and document grounding with vector search
domains.notes: Retrieval-augmented generation on SAP BTP: embeddings, the vector engine / SAP HANA Cloud vector store, document grounding pipelines, chunking and retrieval, and wiring grounding into the Orchestration Service. Building RAG applications that ground LLM answers in SAP and enterprise documents, and evaluating grounding quality and relevance.

extra_guidance: SAP C_AIG_2412 (SAP Certified Associate - Generative AI Developer) is a niche but near-uncontested play - there is almost no quality Udemy prep for it, and the SAP ecosystem (BTP developers, consultants, partners) is a motivated, higher-income audience. Marketing angle: 'the complete, independent prep for SAP's Generative AI Developer certification'. ACCURACY note: the six domain NAMES above are SAP's published blueprint topic areas for C_AIG_2412; SAP publishes relative weight BANDS (e.g., >12%, 8-12%, <8%) rather than exact percentages, so present the weight bands as approximate and direct learners to SAP's official certification page for the current blueprint. CRITICAL format note: the real exam is a System-Based Assessment (SyBA) - a single hands-on, in-system task activity, NOT a classic multiple-choice test - with a 76% pass mark; the course should therefore emphasize doing the actual procedures (configuring Generative AI Hub, building an orchestration pipeline, wiring a prompt template, standing up a RAG/document-grounding flow, calling the Cloud SDK for AI) rather than only trivia, while still using the pipeline's standard MCQ practice questions to reinforce the decisions and steps a SyBA task requires. Generative AI Hub + the Orchestration Service + the SAP Cloud SDK for AI are the through-line. Labs are SAP BTP / AI Launchpad console and SDK read-and-understand walkthroughs (deploy a model in Generative AI Hub, build an orchestration workflow with templating + grounding + content filtering, create a prompt template, implement a RAG pipeline with the HANA Cloud vector store). Cover the classic decisions: Orchestration Service vs direct model calls, prompt registry/templates vs inline prompts, grounding/RAG design and when to use document grounding, content filtering and data masking placement, Python vs JavaScript SDK usage. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation framed around SyBA-style tasks plus time-management. Scan the practice bank for non-SAP cloud-vendor terms before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
